# Deep analysis — what the results say, against the literature, the pipeline, and our findings

**Date:** 2026-09-28 · **Config:** `87f5489e9d59` (lock + deviation 1) · **Code:** `87dcf4f` · **Seeds:** split 2026, bootstrap 20260914
**Companion figure pack:** `figures/extended/` (8 figures, PNG + vector PDF, regenerated by `src/analysis_figures.py`)
**Read with:** `reports/final_results.md`, `reports/limitations.md`, `findings.md`, `literature/literature-review.md`

Every number below was re-derived from the raw artefacts (`results/*.csv`, `features/features.parquet`,
`results/per_image_predictions.parquet`, `data/splits.csv`) before being used. The derivation script
recomputes stored AUROCs from per-image scores, reproduces the group-bootstrap paired CIs, and
re-derives the per-feature statistics; it stops on any mismatch (all checks passed). This document is
therefore safe to quote from in a presentation.

## 1. The verified evidence base

Test set: 600 parent images (300 real, 100 per generator), identical across E1–E5, so every
comparison is paired. AUROC treats generated as positive; brackets are 95 % group-bootstrap CIs.

**Arm comparison (test AUROC):**

| Setting | pixel-pattern (1–7) | frequency (8–14) | combined (1–14) |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 clean (C0), all generators | 0.666 [0.622, 0.707] | 0.752 [0.713, 0.792] | **0.793 [0.759, 0.826]** |
| E1 per generator (each column = that arm) | BigGAN 0.824 · SD 0.581 · ADM 0.591 | BigGAN 0.997 · SD 0.637 · ADM 0.624 | BigGAN 0.990 · SD 0.712 · ADM 0.678 |
| E3 matched JPEG, Δ vs E1 (q90/q75/q50) | −0.005 / −0.016 / −0.025 | +0.003 / +0.005 / +0.014 | −0.007 / −0.003 / +0.000 |
| E2 deliberate mismatch, Δ vs E1 | −0.026 [−0.038, −0.015] | +0.017 [0.009, 0.025] | +0.012 [0.007, 0.017] |
| E4 unseen SD v1.4 (C0) | 0.475 [0.422, 0.541] | 0.560 [0.495, 0.627] | **0.634 [0.578, 0.695]** |
| **E5 unseen SD v1.4 + JPEG q75 (headline)** | 0.465 [0.410, 0.527] | 0.568 [0.505, 0.637] | **0.629 [0.571, 0.690]** |

**Paired effect sizes (group bootstrap, 1,000 rounds, all verified by independent re-derivation):**

| Effect | Δ AUROC | 95 % CI | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1: combined − frequency | +0.041 | [0.018, 0.064] | adding pixel features to frequency helps on seen generators |
| E1: pixel − frequency | −0.087 | [−0.130, −0.046] | frequency alone beats pixel alone |
| E4 − E1 (combined, SD v1.4 held out) | −0.078 | [−0.124, −0.034] | generator shift costs ~8 AUROC points |
| E5 − E4 (combined, + JPEG q75 on unseen) | −0.004 | small | matched compression adds almost nothing on top of shift |
| E5: combined − frequency (unseen SD) | +0.061 | [0.028, 0.094] | the complementarity result (see §4, finding 5) |
| Exploratory: ADM gain when SD removed from training (E4 vs E1) | +0.071 | [0.038, 0.104] | diffusion families interfere with each other |

**Control checks (all pass; the pipeline's integrity evidence):** always-guess 0.500 everywhere;
history-only 0.500 in C0/C1 (pre-processing removes file facts) but 1.000 in E2 by design (the
mismatch is visible to a file-facts classifier); shuffled labels 0.503–0.521 (mean of 200, deviation 1);
pre-receipt file facts alone = 1.000 in every experiment — the dataset-level shortcut, exposed and
excluded from the analysis files.

## 3. Results vs the pipeline (`src/experimental-pipeline.md`, locked v1.0)

- **Stage discipline held.** Stages 0–10 ran in order; the only mid-run stop was the shuffled-label
  control (Stage 8), resolved by owner-approved deviation 1 (200 shuffles, mean gate ±0.03) with a
  written diagnosis (`results/diagnostics/shuffle_control.md`) — no feature, split, classifier, or
  metric changed. This is exactly the "stop on a failed check, fix, rerun" behaviour the spec requires.
- **Locked values were never changed after results.** Resize kernel (bicubic), 256² size, JPEG
  qualities (90/75/50), the 14 feature definitions, the C grid, splits and seeds all appear in
  `config.yaml` exactly as locked; every result table carries the config hash and code version.
- **The pipeline did its job — including against us.** The controls caught the two things a careless
  pipeline would have missed: (a) pre-receipt file facts classify GenImage real vs fake at AUROC 1.000
  (why per-generator rows and matched processing are mandatory); (b) the locked resize itself upsamples
  BigGAN 2×, which is why per-generator rows, not pooled rows, carry the interpretation. A pipeline
  that reports only pooled numbers would have concluded "0.79 AUROC, solved" — the design made the
  shortcut visible instead.
- **Reproducibility.** The 2026-09-27 clean rerun reproduced every `data/` table byte-for-byte and
  every `results/*.csv` exactly; the derivation script in this pack re-derives the statistics a third
  time from the parquet tables.

## 4. The five findings, with their full evidence chains (what we present)

1. **Resizing history beats generation as a signal** (`shortcut_anatomy` figure).
   Evidence: at C0, BigGAN is separated near-perfectly by every high-frequency statistic (univariate
   AUROC 0.004–0.03, i.e. ≥ 0.97 reversed) while the diffusion families are not (0.33–0.62); the
   classifier-level gap matches (BigGAN 0.99 vs SD/ADM 0.68–0.71 combined). The locked bicubic
   128→256 upsample empties the top half of BigGAN's spectrum. This is our feature-level instance of
   the upsampling artifacts literature [5], [7], [8] — with the twist that here the pipeline, not the
   generator, created the trace.
2. **Matched JPEG hardly matters once the classifier is refit** (`robustness_curves` + `degradation_path`).
   |Δ| ≤ 0.025 AUROC over q90→q50 across all arms; E5−E4 = −0.004. Consistent with [11] once data
   handling is matched; distinct from the test-time-JPEG drop, which we did not measure (limitation 8).
3. **Feature meaning can flip while the classifier score stays put** (`f11_reversal`, `effect_size_heatmap`).
   f11's Cohen's d goes +0.80 (C0) → −0.26 (q50) and its BigGAN univariate AUROC goes 0.009 → 0.772,
   yet pooled classifier AUROC moves +0.000. "Values changed" and "classification changed" are
   different findings — H3's two-verdict design caught a case where they come apart.
4. **Stable is not useful** (`stability_vs_separation` + heatmap row f14). f14 is the most stable
   frequency feature (0.003 SD) and carries no signal anywhere (0.497). Stability must not be read as
   robustness-of-signal.
5. **Arms are complementary on an unseen generator** (`arm_complementarity`, `roc_headline` right panel).
   Pixel alone is at chance on held-out SD v1.4 (0.465) yet adding the 7 pixel features to the
   frequency set raises AUROC by +0.061 [0.028, 0.094]. At the validation threshold the arms flag
   different fakes (pixel 34/100, frequency 19/100, union 41/100, both missed 59/100). Supports [15],
   [16]: local pixel statistics carry signal that frequency statistics miss, and vice versa.

## 5. Results vs the literature — position of the study

**We confirm, at feature level, what the fairness literature showed at detector level.** Grommelt et
al. [1] and B-Free [2] showed detectors exploit processing-history differences; our pre-receipt control
(1.000) and the BigGAN resize shortcut show the same at the level of individual statistics — a per
-feature version of their result, which neither paper reports.

**We confirm generator shift [11], [12] with magnitudes for simple features:** −0.078 [−0.124, −0.034]
(combined) when SD v1.4 is held out, and the pixel arm collapses to chance. Also the interference
finding (ADM +0.071 when SD leaves training) is a within-diffusion version of [12]'s family-dependence.

**We add what the retrieved literature does not report** (careful wording: "no retrieved abstract
reports this exact protocol"): per-feature stability vs separation under matched JPEG as two separate
verdicts; a documented case where a feature's meaning flips under compression while classification is
unchanged (f11); and a joint matched-JPEG × unseen-generator × per-feature comparison under one
pre-registered protocol with leakage controls. Before any stronger novelty wording: full reads of
Grommelt [1] and Sato [10] are still required (README rule).

**We do not contradict anything.** Dong et al. [9]'s caution ("spectral traces can be weakened") is
supported from a new angle — the trace we found was created by processing, and compression changed it.

## 6. What we can and cannot say (claim discipline for the presentation)

**Can say (all CI-backed):**
- "Under one locked, pre-registered pipeline with matched processing and group splits, the combined
  14-feature set separated real from generated images best in every tested setting."
- "On the held-out generator under matched JPEG q75 (headline): AUROC 0.629 [0.571, 0.690]; the
  pixel-pattern arm alone is not above chance."
- "The pooled 0.79 is dominated by one resizing shortcut; on the two diffusion families the best simple
  set reaches 0.63–0.76."
- "Matched JPEG (refit per condition) changed separation by at most 0.025 AUROC between q90 and q50."
- "A feature's direction of separation can reverse under compression while classifier performance is
  essentially unchanged."
- "H1 supported; H2 partly supported; H3 supported in an unexpected form; H4 supported for SD v1.4;
  H5 not tested."

**Cannot say (and why):**
- Not "these features detect AI-generated images" — separation may partly measure prior JPEG history of
  reals and resizing of fakes (limitations 2–3).
- Not "robust to JPEG" in the transfer sense — classifiers were refit per condition (limitation 8).
- Not "generator shift always costs X" — one held-out family only (limitation 4).
- Not "first" / "state of the art" — novelty wording is fixed as above; no SOTA comparison was run.
- Not anything about generators, datasets, encoders, or quality levels outside {BigGAN, SD v1.4, ADM},
  {GenImage val}, {Pillow 4:2:0}, {90, 75, 50} (limitation 1).

**Limitations to state up front in any presentation:** pre-receipt history shortcut (1.000); BigGAN 2×
upsample inflating pooled numbers; single unseen fold; content bias not tested; mirror sampling.
